hints: Each query asks how many times a path uses each node.
For path u-v with l=LCA(u,v), add +1 at u and v, subtract 1 at l, and subtract 1 at parent(l).
After all queries, accumulate counts from children to parents.
analogy: Path endpoints add flow upward until their routes meet at the LCA; the two subtractions prevent counting the meeting point twice.
example: For path 4-5 with LCA 2, marks at 4,5 and -1 at 2 and parent(2) make the final count 1 on 4,2,5.
algorithm: Apply the four difference updates per path using LCA, then postorder-sum each node's value into its parent. The resulting node total is the number of queried paths passing through it.
correctness: For each path, the endpoint contributions cancel above the LCA and leave one unit on exactly the nodes along u-v; summing queries combines their counts.
complexity: O((n+q) log n) time and O(n+q) space.
